checks.title: Platform database backups on the host
checks.rationale: The platform's own database holds every project, server, secret and key it manages; losing it means rebuilding all of it by hand. Coolify keeps local backups under /data/coolify/backups; Dokploy sends backups to S3 destinations only. A local copy alone is not a backup: keep one off the server, and keep the platform's app key somewhere else, since the database is useless without it.
checks.fix: Schedule backups of the platform database to off site storage and test a restore; store the app key outside the server.

checks.title: Backup tools present
checks.rationale: restic, borg, borgmatic, kopia and rclone configs or binaries are a sign host level backups exist. Their configs often hold repository passwords and cloud credentials, so stackward records only that they exist. A backup nobody has restored is a hope, not a backup.
checks.verify: command -v restic borg borgmatic kopia rclone; ls -l /etc/borgmatic* /etc/restic ~/.config/rclone
checks.fix: Run a restore test into a scratch folder and write down how long it took.
